artifacts.title: LFI log poisoning to base64 password and VNC root (Poison)
artifacts.starting_access: unauthenticated web access to Apache/PHP on a FreeBSD host
artifacts.outcome: root via a root VNC session
transferable_properties: search for logs when PHP code can be executed to poison them
LFI to log poisoning upgrades file read into RCE
base64-encoded passwords may be encoded many times, decode repeatedly
search for root-owned processes, VNC sessions are a good entry point
forward localhost-only VNC ports over SSH

hypotheses.statement: LFI to log poisoning gives RCE

selected_action.intent: poison the Apache access log with a PHP payload and execute it via LFI

evidence.summary: injected a PHP webshell into the User-Agent, parsed the log via LFI, and got RCE

observations: pwdbackup.txt contains a base64 password encoded 13 times

hypotheses.statement: decoding the base64 13 times yields a usable system password

selected_action.intent: decode the password repeatedly and try it over SSH as charix

evidence.summary: decoded the password and logged in over SSH as charix, obtaining the user flag

observations: a VNC server runs as root but only on localhost
secret.zip in charix home holds the VNC password

hypotheses.statement: forwarding the VNC port and using the extracted password gives a root VNC session

selected_action.intent: forward the VNC port over SSH and connect with the extracted password

evidence.summary: connected to the root VNC session and obtained the root flag
